newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican calls meeting of Great Lakes' bishops.
newsitem.headline: Vatican calls meeting of Great Lakes' bishops.

text.p: The Vatican said on Tuesday it had convened a meeting of Roman Catholic bishops from Africa's Great Lakes region to discuss the area's humanitarian crisis.
Cardinal Roger Ethegaray, head of the Vatican Pontifical Council on Justice and Peace, told a news conference he would chair the four-day meeting beginning on Wednesday in Nairobi.
Noting that several Catholic priests had been killed in ethnic violence in the Great Lakes region, the cardinal said the meeting was being held outside the area for security reasons.
"Faced with enormous social problems, the meeting is essential to analyse the situation and to identify priorities and actions of the Church," he said.
"The meeting also wants to be a sign of ecclesiastic unity which is able to survive the damage provoked by the conflicts and in that way to contribute to reconciliation."

He said all the bishops of Burundi and Rwanda would attend as well as several bishops from Zaire and Church representatives from Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda. It would would be the first time in four years that all bishops from the region had met.

Pope John Paul, responding to allegations that Roman Catholic nuns and priests took part in Rwanda's 1994 genocide, in which one million minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus were killed, has said the Church could not be held responsible.

"All members of the Church who sinned during the genocide must have the courage to bear the consequences of the acts they committed against God and their fellow men," the Pope said in a recent letter to Rwanda's amabassador to the Vatican.

But he said the Roman Catholic Church as an institution "could not be held responsible for the blame of these members...who acted against the law of the Gospel. They will be called to account for their actions."

The Pope told the ambassador that as hundreds of thousands of refugees were now returning home from Zaire, there was an urgent need for Rwandans to seek national unity and erase "the resentment in their hearts."
